title: Spec: GCP-6.5 slot-claim text fixes (header hex, key 7 ordinal, receiver-cache normative)
description:
Fix GCP-6.5 spec text bugs and close the receiver-side claim_seq spec gap, so the C/Python/Rust children implement one unambiguous format.

Changes (all in spec/08-gateway-coordination.md):

1. Protected-header example bug, spec/08:135. The example h'a10139ffff' decodes to {1: -65536}, contradicting the stated {1: -65537} on the same line and the alg ID used by capability announcements (python/src/lichen/crypto/capability_announcements.py) and GCP-7.1. Verified with cbor2: canonical {1: -65537} = a1 01 3a 00010000; bstr-wrapped = h'47A1013A00010000'. Replace the example bytes; note that -65536 is a decoy that verification MUST reject (wrong alg).

2. Payload table extension, spec/08:142-164: add key 7: ordinal (uint) — the claiming gateway's ordinal position (interleaved mode, per 6.2). Evidence that receivers consume it: lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_slot_coord.c:376 passes claim->ordinal into lichen_slot_coord_register_gateway. gateway_count and slot_start stay sender-local (no receiver consumer) — state that explicitly so implementers do not add them.

3. Receiver-side claim_seq cache persistence, spec/08:193,210-220: the persistence table ( Gateway boot / Before claim / Receive claim ) is written from the claiming gateway's perspective. Add normative text: the RECEIVING coordinator MUST also persist the per-gateway claim_seq high-water in non-volatile storage, keyed by gateway IID; reject claim_seq <= cached (6.5 step 8); persist the new high-water BEFORE applying the claim to the slot table (crash between apply and persist would reopen the replay window; persist-first only burns a sequence number, forcing the legit sender to increment per the Before claim row).

4. On-air size guidance: add a note that a COSE_Sign1 slot claim is ~114 B typical (4 slots) / ~227 B at the 60-slot cap (CONFIG_LICHEN_SLOT_COORD_MAX_SLOTS, lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/include/lichen/coap_slot_coord.h:38), which does not fit a 255-byte LoRa PHY payload (spec/02a:21) once CoAP+OSCORE+SCHC headers (~25-45 B) are added. On-LoRa claims SHOULD cap at ~40 slots; larger allocations use backbone transport.

5. Response-code alignment inside 6.5 validation steps (spec/08:184-199): step 10 says 2.04 Changed, step 11 says 4.09 Conflict with winning gateway's claim — keep as-is in spec; the C child aligns code. Add one sentence mapping replay/expiry/invalid-slot failures to 4.03 Forbidden per :198, and reiterate silent-discard (return 0, no CoAP response) for invalid/missing signatures per :199 with rate-limited WARN logging requirement.

Acceptance criteria:
- spec/08:135 example bytes encode {1: -65537} (checkable with cbor2.dumps(canonical=True)).
- Payload table lists keys 1-7 with types; explicit note that gateway_count/slot_start are not carried.
- Receiver-side NV persistence is normative (MUST), with persist-before-apply ordering stated.
- On-air size note with the 40-slot SHOULD cap and the 255-byte reference.
- No change to the COSE_Sign1 envelope shape, Sig_structure, or the SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)) signing input (spec/08:171-177 stands).
close_reason: All 5 changes landed in spec/08-gateway-coordination.md (only file touched): (1) :135 example now h'47A1013A00010000' — bstr-wrapped canonical {1: -65537}, chosen because COSE_Sign1 array element 1 is a bstr per RFC 9052 and the Python precedent (capability_announcements.py cose_sign1=[protected_raw_map_bytes,...] CBOR-encodes it as bstr); cbor2 verification: cbor2.dumps({1:-65537},canonical=True).hex()='a1013a00010000', bstr-wrapped='47a1013a00010000'; decoy note added (-65536 / h'a10139ffff' MUST be rejected per step 4). (2) Payload table key 7 ordinal (uint) added to CBOR block + table, receivers-consume note citing lichen_slot_coord_register_gateway(); explicit note gateway_count/slot_start are sender-local, MUST NOT be added (verified no receiver consumer in coap_slot_coord.c — only claim->ordinal is passed through). (3) Receiver-side persistence: 'Receive claim' table row amended + normative paragraph — receiving coordinator MUST persist per-gateway claim_seq high-water in NVS keyed by gateway IID, reject claim_seq <= cached (step 8), persist BEFORE applying to slot table, persist-first rationale (burns a seq number vs reopening replay window) stated explicitly. (4) On-air size note: recomputed with cbor2 against the key-7 payload — 105-109 B typical 4 slots (wrote ~110), 198-222 B at 60-slot cap (wrote ~220; bead estimated 114/227 — within ~2-8%, not material, used my numbers); 255-byte PHY reference to spec/02a (255-byte limit actually at spec/02a §2a.2 line 111, bead's :21 had drifted); CoAP+OSCORE+SCHC ~25-45 B overhead; 60-slot does not reliably fit (222+45=267>255); LoRa claims SHOULD cap at ~40 slots (~180 B; 178+45=223<=255). (5) Response-code alignment: sentence mapping replay(step 8)/expiry(step 7)/invalid-slot(step 9) to 4.03 Forbidden; silent-discard reiterated as return 0 + no CoAP response + rate-limited WARN logging. Acceptance criteria all met; Sig_structure/envelope/signing-input block verified undisturbed (git grep shows 08:171-177 content verbatim, now at :190-202 after insertions). Follow-up bead project-LICHEN-worker6-5brg filed: GCP-7.1 handoff examples (:295,:334) have the identical decoy-hex bug, left out of this bead's 5-change scope.
